evidence.reason: The `identity is None` path unconditionally runs `systemctl --user stop` even when `_show_scope` reported `LoadState=not-found`, and also when the scope exists with an empty cgroup, because the member ownership check is skipped in those cases. A boot in another state directory with the same run id can create the same `crq-vm-<run_id>.scope` between that query and the stop, so directory A can stop directory B's live guest. The code comment itself acknowledges that another workspace can own a scope with the same name, so this is an implementation race, not an accepted limitation. The smallest compatible fix is to skip `stop` for absent or empty scopes and rely on the post-stop state check to fail closed; tying scope names to the canonical run directory would be an additional hardening change, not required for this correction.
